entries.rationale: Account editing runtime ownership is canonical.
Authentication context and policy ownership is canonical.
Neuro-commenting router, contracts, workflow metadata, and public facades are canonical.
Known wrappers preserve public import compatibility and must remain behavior-free.
entries.removal_condition: Remove only after import/reference audit proves no downstream users and replacement paths are stable.

entries.rationale: Account-adjacent APIs, services, and DTOs are broad production feature surfaces outside canonical modules.
entries.removal_condition: Each account-owned feature surface is either assigned to a canonical module or documented as shared platform infrastructure.
entries.target_owner: future account modules or documented shared account platform

entries.rationale: Lifecycle API and service ownership remains global while runtime role metadata already reserves account_lifecycle_jobs.
entries.removal_condition: Deletion/export flows are module-owned with preserved preview/request/export/audit semantics; legacy paths are wrappers-only or removed after reference audit.

entries.rationale: Safety gate and override behavior is cross-feature policy code without a canonical module boundary.
entries.removal_condition: Account safety exposes public gate/readiness/override contracts and consumers use that boundary instead of internal services.

entries.rationale: Onboarding feature paths are global production feature surfaces.
entries.removal_condition: Bought-account onboarding is module-owned or explicitly retained as account platform debt.

entries.rationale: Human behavior emulation is feature logic outside app.modules.
entries.removal_condition: Human-behavior policy/runtime surfaces are module-owned or explicitly classified as shared policy infrastructure.
entries.target_owner: app.modules.human_behavior or documented shared policy boundary

entries.rationale: Story feature code has API and service ownership outside app.modules.
entries.removal_condition: Story draft/post/capability ownership is either module-owned or explicitly tracked as approved debt.

entries.rationale: Module metadata, registry, and non-runtime template support module governance.
Worker processes, queue declarations, and scheduling/reaper paths are execution infrastructure.
Global schemas and ORM models remain transitional shared ownership surfaces.
entries.removal_condition: DTO and ORM ownership is either module-owned, shared-contract-owned, or documented as compatibility debt.

entries.rationale: Cross-cutting auth, storage, runtime, audit, notification, tenant, and operator support code is not a bounded feature module by itself.
Supporting audit, tests, docs, memory, and frontend ownership evidence are tracked separately from backend production domains.

scope.classification_rule: Every discovered zone is classified as canonical_feature_module, unmanaged_feature_surface, shared_platform_infrastructure, compatibility_wrapper, runtime_process_ownership, or supporting_tool_test_documentation_frontend_evidence.

findings.evidence: app.modules.registry imports account_editing, auth, neuro_commenting, warmup; open unmanaged feature surfaces: debt-account-safety.
findings.finding: Backend has canonical modules, but high-risk feature ownership still exists outside app.modules.
findings.recommendation: Complete Phase 0 guard, then migrate neuro_commenting, account_safety, and account_lifecycle in separate PRs.
findings.risk: High. Architecture audit must not report overall backend GREEN while high-risk unmanaged domains remain.

findings.evidence: apps/dashboard/src/modules has account-editing, auth, warmup, and shared indexes; frontend-ownership-audit.md records migrated and deferred surfaces.
findings.finding: Frontend modularization is progressing, but global lib, hooks, components, and features still own substantial feature logic.
findings.recommendation: Continue moving feature-specific dashboard helpers/components into modules in small compatibility-preserving passes.
findings.risk: Future frontend work can bypass module boundaries unless feature ownership keeps moving behind public module indexes.

findings.evidence: backend/app/contracts exists for low-risk shared DTOs; app.schemas re-exports moved DTOs for compatibility.
findings.finding: Shared contracts extraction has started while app.schemas.py remains a compatibility/global DTO layer.
findings.recommendation: Move only proven shared DTOs into app.contracts and continue keeping ORM access behind repositories before splitting app.models.
findings.risk: Remaining DTOs in app.schemas.py can still attract new shared imports unless architecture tests keep enforcing boundaries.

findings.evidence: Wrappers include compatibility docstrings and are documented in legacy-wrapper-audit.md, legacy-wrapper-deprecation-plan.md, and legacy-wrappers.json.
findings.finding: Legacy API/service/worker wrappers remain import-compatible with a static deprecation plan.
findings.recommendation: Advance stages only in dedicated compatibility-preserving PRs; do not remove wrappers before Stage 5.
findings.risk: Low while architecture tests prevent modules from importing legacy wrappers.

findings.evidence: Runtime role metadata maps each reserved queue to a dedicated worker role; maintenance_worker maps only to maintenance_jobs.
findings.finding: Reserved queue ownership is logically split into dedicated runtime roles.
findings.recommendation: Keep logical roles narrow and split physical worker services only when production resources allow it.
findings.risk: Low. Resource-constrained staging may still group queues in one physical worker by using raw --queues mode without --role.

findings.evidence: Multiple tests parse imports and source files independently with small local helper functions.
findings.finding: Architecture tests contain duplicated static-analysis helper patterns.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate AST/import helper utilities after the boundary set stabilizes.
findings.risk: Low. Duplication can make future boundary-rule changes noisy.

findings.evidence: CI, Test Quality, Semgrep, Secrets Scan, SBOM, Trivy, Complexity, Gitleaks config, and security docs exist.
findings.finding: Security baseline workflows and documentation are present.
findings.recommendation: Keep security docs in sync with GitHub branch protection and workflow policy changes.
findings.risk: Low. Branch protection remains a repository setting outside source control.

findings.finding: Machine-readable inventory tracks backend/app feature surfaces outside canonical modules.
findings.recommendation: Keep architecture debt inventory exhaustive and fail checks on untracked backend/app production files.
findings.risk: High if new feature-owned code can appear outside app.modules without being classified as debt or platform support.
